title: Module quiz: One REST API under every SDK

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A hand-written client and an SDK client call the API from the same service. After the provider adds a new stop reason value, only the hand-written client starts failing. Which cause is most likely?

options.text: It has no retries, which the SDK would have supplied automatically
options.says: Ruled out because a retry cannot cure a parse failure, and "retrying does not help: the proxy answers the same page again" shows the same logic for a repeated reply.

options.text: Its logic assumes that the set of labels it saw is complete
options.says: A client that fails on an unknown value breaks "on a change the versioning page allows", and the page says a stop reason is among the values "you do not know" that must be tolerated, not only a field.

options.text: It lacks the identifying platform headers that the SDK sends
options.says: Ruled out because the SDK's extra headers "help debugging and are not part of your contract".

options.text: It was written against an older revision of the contract header
options.says: Ruled out because "the only current value of anthropic-version is 2023-06-01", and an older one "may be unavailable for new users".

questions.stem: A service builds a new SDK client for every streamed call, and its latency and open-socket count grow under load. Which change is best?

options.text: Keep a single instance created at start-up and let every request handler share it
options.says: The page says to create one client and share it, because "a new client means a new connection pool each time".

options.text: Move the calls to a websocket so that one connection is kept open
options.says: Ruled out because "a websocket adds an upgrade, a session to restore and trouble at every proxy, and gives nothing in return".

options.text: Turn streaming off so that fewer sockets are used by each of the calls
options.says: Ruled out because streaming is what keeps long calls from being dropped as idle: "Bytes keep flowing, and the connection is not idle".

options.text: Raise the output limit so that fewer calls are needed for the same work
options.says: Ruled out because "the cost shows up as latency and sockets" and comes from the number of clients, which the output limit does not change.

questions.stem: A call that asks for incremental output returns 200 and a few events, and then the network drops. A developer records the call as successful because of the 200. What should the page's reader tell them?

options.text: The code shows only that the reply began, so the end must be checked as well
options.says: The page's second trap says "a 200 does not mean the answer is complete", so the end of the stream has to be checked as well.

options.text: The code is final, since the server sends it after the whole message is written
options.says: Ruled out because "the connection stays open until the message is complete", so the status comes first.

options.text: The events already received form a complete message and can be stored as the result
options.says: Ruled out because "a streamed reply can start with a 200 and still end with an error event".

options.text: The call needs a longer timeout value so that the code can arrive before the drop
options.says: Ruled out because "some networks may drop idle connections after a variable period of time", and a longer timeout on your side does not stop a drop.

questions.stem: A team must report a failing call to the provider's support while keeping its logs free of secrets and customer text. Which record should the service keep for each call?

options.text: The authorization header and the body, so that the call can be reproduced
options.says: Ruled out because an error message that is logged "is read by people who must not see a key", and a header would carry the key.

options.text: The complete request and reply, so that support staff can replay them
options.says: Ruled out because "customer text does not belong in a log by default".

options.text: The request id, the status and the error type, without bodies or keys
options.says: The request id is what support asks for: "include it when you contact support about a specific request", and the status and type classify the failure.

options.text: Only the time of the call, since the provider can find the call from it
options.says: Ruled out because the documentation says to "include it when you contact support about a specific request", and a time stamp is not that id.
